standard_prerequisites.name: Cardinal numbers
standard_prerequisites.statement: card is the set-truncation of the type of sets, with cd(A) the cardinal of a set A, and 0 := cd(empty), 1 := cd(unit).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the structure whose semiring laws are asserted.

standard_prerequisites.name: Univalence
standard_prerequisites.statement: Two sets are equal as soon as they are equivalent.
standard_prerequisites.use: It reduces a cardinal identity to an equivalence of sets at source line 748.

standard_prerequisites.name: Induction on the set-truncation
standard_prerequisites.statement: To prove a statement about elements of a set-truncation it suffices to prove it for the images cd(A).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the reduction to representatives at source line 746.

core_obligations: Prove one representative law, commutativity of multiplication, noting that every other law is exactly analogous (source line 744).

Observe that the goal alpha beta = beta alpha is a mere proposition, indeed a set, because card is a set, so by induction it suffices to treat alpha and beta of the form cd(A) and cd(B) (source lines 745-746).
Rewrite cd(A) cd(B) and cd(B) cd(A) by their definitions as cd(A x B) and cd(B x A), reducing the goal to A x B = B x A (source line 747).
Apply univalence to reduce further to an equivalence A x B ~ B x A and supply the swapping map with its inverse (source lines 748-749).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce the general law to representatives by the set-ness of card.
Unfold the operations, apply univalence and exhibit the swapping equivalence.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 10.2.4 at source lines 730-742: the cardinal numbers form a commutative semiring, with all seven displayed laws. The author's proof (source lines 743-750) proves multiplication commutativity and declares the rest analogous, but the proof of that one law is a chain of reductions that consumes three separate facts: because card is a set the goal is a mere proposition, so induction reduces it to cardinals of sets (lines 745-746); the definitions of the operations then rewrite the goal as an identity between cd(A x B) and cd(B x A) (line 747); and univalence turns that identity into the requirement of an equivalence between the products, which is supplied by the swapping map (lines 748-749). The statement lists the seven laws and hides that the reduction passes through truncation induction, definitional unfolding and univalence.
